title: Adaptive SLO-driven retry and hedging contract with idempotency headers
creator: Ava Miller
description: Goal: Define and implement a unified, SLO-driven retry + hedging contract across Redwood services and SDKs that preserves correctness for non-idempotent operations via a standard idempotency header and server-side deduplication window. Background: Current teams use different retry/backoff defaults and ad-hoc idempotency headers; hedged requests exist only in a few runtime paths. This causes inconsistent user-visible latency, duplicated side-effects, and brittle multi-region failover behavior. This ticket specifies a contract (server + SDK) covering: 1) Idempotency header semantics (X-Redwood-Idempotency or Idempotency-Key), TTL, conflict behavior, and server dedupe guarantees. 2) SLO-driven retry policy: mapping from route-level SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency and error budget) to retry budget, max attempts, and exponential-jitter backoff parameters. 3) Hedged requests behavior specifically for P99-driven latency tails and multi-region failover: when to issue hedges, cancellation semantics, and limits. 4) Circuit breaker integration and load-shedding rules to prevent amplification; how hedging interacts with CB states. 5) SDK contract: how clients generate/propagate idempotency keys, optional opt-outs, automatic hedging toggles, and telemetry. 6) Migrations, rollout, monitoring, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts and validates a standard idempotency header: 'Idempotency-Key' or 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' with documented semantics
Server maintains a configurable deduplication window (default 24h) and returns consistent conflict errors when duplicate non-idempotent attempts are detected
SDKs implement automatic idempotency key generation for write operations unless opt-out header present
Route-level SLOs are mapped to retry budgets and default backoff policy (base=50ms, max_backoff=2s, max_attempts=3) and can be overridden by service owners
Hedged requests are enabled behind a feature flag and triggered only when tail latency risk exceeds configured SLO thresholds; hedges are limited to 1 extra replica by default
Circuit breaker states disable hedging for routes in 'open' state and cause SDKs to fall back to single-attempt with backoff
Observability: new metrics exist (hedged_requests_total, hedged_successes, idempotency_conflict_count, retry_budget_consumed) and dashboards updated
Integration tests cover multi-region hedging + dedupe for write and read paths, demonstrating no duplicate side-effects in 99.999% of runs
testing_plan: Unit tests: validation of idempotency header parsing, TTL expiry, and conflict mapping
Integration tests: two-region test harness that simulates delayed primary-region responses and verifies hedged success behavior and dedupe of writes
Chaos tests: circuit-breaker open state + high-error injection to ensure hedging is suppressed and system degrades per runbook
Load tests: ensure hedging cannot increase peak QPS beyond configured capacity; measure amplification ratio
SDK E2E: language SDKs (Go, Python, Typescript) use generated idempotency keys and opt-out patterns; CI runs against staging runtime feature flag
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Spec + API: final signoff on contract and conformance tests (this ticket). Create feature flag 'hedging-v2' and 'idempotency-standard'
Phase 1 - Server-side: implement idempotency header parsing, storage TTL, conflict error types; expose route-level retry config in runtime metadata
Phase 2 - SDKs: add automatic idempotency key generation with opt-out, expose hedging toggle in SDK config; default disabled in GA until telemetry baseline is stable
Phase 3 - Canary + Observability: enable hedging-v2 for low-traffic customers and internal canaries; monitor metrics and error budgets for 72h before wider rollout
Phase 4 - Region-aware hedges: enable multi-region hedging for read-favoring routes where cross-region dedupe is safe; ensure routing and RBAC constraints honored
Phase 5 - Post-GA: iterate defaults based on telemetry and make route-level policies editable in Console
